note: Hook formulas for Facebook Reels and video. Each match regex was written against how people actually talk, not against the template. Edit freely. hookscore.py and swipe.py both read this file.

formulas.name: Cost Confession
formulas.template: I lost {amount} because of {one specific mistake}.
formulas.example: I lost $18,000 because of one missing contract clause.
formulas.for: Stories with a real loss. The loss is the hook, the fix is the payoff.
formulas.ruined_by: Vague amounts ('a lot of money') or a loss that is not actually yours.

formulas.name: Time Collapse
formulas.template: {Task} used to take me {long time}. Now it takes {short time}.
formulas.example: Invoices used to take me a whole Sunday. Now it's ten minutes.
formulas.for: Process wins. The ratio does the work.
formulas.ruined_by: A ratio nobody believes, or no proof in the body.

formulas.name: Nobody Tells You
formulas.example: Nobody tells you your first 30 videos are supposed to flop.
formulas.ruined_by: A truth everybody already says.

formulas.name: Contrarian Flip
formulas.template: {Common advice} is wrong. Here's what to do instead.
formulas.example: Posting every day is why your Page is dying.
formulas.for: Positions. Needs a real reason in the next line.
formulas.ruined_by: Disagreeing for attention and then agreeing in the body.

formulas.name: The Statistic
formulas.example: 80% of the people who message my Page never get a reply.
formulas.ruined_by: A made-up statistic. Never invent one.

formulas.name: The Reveal
formulas.example: This is the exact menu card that doubled our Friday orders.
formulas.for: Showing the object on camera in frame one.
formulas.ruined_by: Not showing the thing.

formulas.name: Someone Else's Result
formulas.example: My neighbour sold 40 cakes in a day off one Facebook Group post.
formulas.for: Borrowed proof. Real and attributed, with permission.
formulas.ruined_by: An anonymous 'one client' that might not exist.

formulas.name: The Superlative
formulas.example: The cheapest marketing I ever did was answering every comment.
formulas.ruined_by: 'Best ever' with no specifics.

formulas.name: The Steal
formulas.example: Steal the three-line reply that books half my appointments.
formulas.ruined_by: Nothing worth stealing in the body.

formulas.name: The Mistake List
formulas.example: Three mistakes that cost my shop its first year.
formulas.for: Experience. Each mistake is one beat.
formulas.ruined_by: Generic mistakes everyone lists.

formulas.name: Before / After
formulas.example: Twelve likes a post in March. Four thousand shares in June.
formulas.ruined_by: No before shown.

formulas.name: The Question They Google
formulas.example: How much should a wedding photographer in Kathmandu charge?
formulas.ruined_by: A question you do not answer in the first 10 seconds.
formulas.match: (?i)^(how much|how do (i|you)|how to|what('s| is) the (best|right)|should (i|you)|is it worth|why does|why do)\b

formulas.name: Warning
formulas.example: If your Page bio still says 'welcome to our page', you're losing customers.
formulas.ruined_by: Fear with no fix.

formulas.name: Story Drop-In
formulas.example: The landlord called at 6am and said we had two weeks to leave.
formulas.for: Narrative Reels. Start in the middle.
formulas.ruined_by: Starting at the beginning of the story.

formulas.name: Price Tag
formulas.template: This {thing} cost {price}. Was it worth it?
formulas.example: This espresso machine cost me 90,000 rupees. Here's the honest math.
formulas.ruined_by: Hiding the verdict until the end.

formulas.name: Myth vs Fact
formulas.example: You've been told to post at 9am. My best posts went out at 11pm.
formulas.ruined_by: A fact you cannot back up.
formulas.match: (?i)\b(you'?ve been told|they told you|everyone says|everybody says|myth)\b

formulas.name: Insider Line
formulas.template: As a {role}, here's what I'd never {do}.
formulas.example: I've been a mechanic 15 years. I'd never buy this car.
formulas.ruined_by: Authority you do not have.
formulas.match: (?i)\b(as a|i'?ve been an?|i worked as an?|i'?m an?) .{2,30}(and|,|\.)?.{0,20}\b(never|always|here'?s)\b

formulas.name: Countdown
formulas.example: Four free tools that run my whole bakery. The last one replaced my accountant.
formulas.for: Lists where one item is the payoff.
formulas.ruined_by: Padding to hit a round number.

formulas.name: Direct Challenge
formulas.template: You're {doing X} wrong, and it's costing you {Y}.
formulas.example: You're pricing by the hour, and it's costing you every repeat client.
formulas.ruined_by: Sounding smug. The cost has to be specific.

formulas.name: Overheard
formulas.example: "Why is your Page more trusted than our website?" a customer asked me.
formulas.ruined_by: A quote nobody said.

formulas.name: The Test
formulas.template: I tried {thing} for {time}. Here's what happened.
formulas.example: I answered every Facebook comment within an hour for 30 days.
formulas.ruined_by: An experiment you didn't finish.

formulas.name: Local Angle
formulas.template: If you live in {place}, {specific useful thing}.
formulas.example: If you live in Pokhara, this is the only tailor open on Saturdays.
formulas.for: Facebook's strength: local audiences, Groups, Marketplace.
formulas.ruined_by: A place name bolted onto generic advice.
formulas.match: (?i)\b(if you live in|anyone in|people in|locals? in|in (my|our) (town|city|area|neighbou?rhood))\b

formulas.name: Family Truth
formulas.example: My dad ran his shop for 30 years without a website. Here's why it worked.
formulas.ruined_by: Sentimentality with no point.

formulas.name: Unpopular Opinion
formulas.example: Unpopular opinion: your shop doesn't need Instagram. It needs a Facebook Group.
formulas.ruined_by: A popular opinion wearing the label.

dealbreakers.why: Greeting. Nobody opened Facebook to be greeted.
Opens with "stop scrolling". Asking for attention proves you have not earned it.

dealbreakers.regex: (?i)\b(in (this|today'?s) (video|reel|post)|today i'?m going to|i'?m going to (show|teach|tell) you|welcome back)\b
dealbreakers.why: Preamble. The video starts at the sentence you'd reach at second six.
Retention bait. Facebook reads the drop-off anyway.
"Did you know" signals trivia, and the answer is usually yes.
Engagement bait. Meta demotes posts that ask for reactions, shares, tags or comments as a trade.
